headline.why: The headline and lede, both visible before scrolling, name the tool (Oxlint + oxfmt), give 44.0 s → 5.3 s, state the cost (alpha JS plugins, 1 rule dropped, 3 path checks) and the Biome comparison (163 of 295). They also correct the 'oxprettier' name, and the hero bar chart is to scale. However, 'and 263 rules keep working' overclaims: one migrated rule crashes and has to be switched off.

accuracy.why: Mostly faithful: keeps/loses/fix-first lists, Biome gaps, the oxfmt-first path and 'what would change' all match facts.md. There are some overclaims. '263 rules keep working' ignores the crashing react-x rule and the new false positives. 'Oxlint runs the same lint in 5.3 s' is not quite true, because 5.3 s was measured after dropping a rule and with the selectors missing. 'Oxlint's React … rules run as alpha JS plugins' is wrong because eslint-plugin-react is built in; only react-x and react-jsx are JS plugins. Saying the 2.3 s oxfmt check took place 'against Prettier' leaves out that the run flagged 1,028 files because of CRLF.

numbers.why: All figures match facts.md: 44.0, 5.3, 3.3, 263/276, 163/295 (55 %), 132 lost, 98 + 34, 190 files, 2.3 s vs 10.2 s, 3 code files, 25 files, 149 drifted, 1,028, ~203 disables, and the 47.3 s and 4.75–4.92 s corroborating runs. The page notes that the rule-count bases differ and that warm-cache timing was not measured. One small issue: the migrator bars set 263/276 next to 163/295 as lengths on a shared absolute scale, which invites comparing different bases.

story.why: The story has a clear arc (today → gap → Oxlint → Biome → catch → safe first step) and one sticky graphic that builds up step by step: ESLint bar, then Oxlint, then Biome, then rule bars. The lint bars are to scale. The final step only adds a text line for oxfmt vs Prettier rather than a visual, and the 'catch' marker isn't visible in the final shot. Navigation labels lag behind the active step (the phone header shows 'Story · Oxlint' while the Biome step is active).

decision.why: Three options, with A recommended and C as the cautious choice. Each has keeps/loses/fix-first/risks/effort in days, and there is a concrete 'what would change this' list. Risks come with fixes such as pinning versions and adding .gitattributes. B's risks are mostly restated losses, and the open decisions (RuleTester port, format:check) are only partly covered.

concision.why: Around 1,100 words, the answer comes immediately, and details sit in the option panels and the methods section. Some numbers repeat across the hero, story and option chips (44.0/5.3/3.3, 263, 163/295, 2.3 vs 10.2), but not excessively. Nothing a decision needs is missing.

visual.why: Clean, legible layout in both themes and on the phone, with to-scale bars and a sticky graphic that works on mobile. The story chapter has large empty areas on desktop. The decision detail panel only shows one option at a time. The nav highlight doesn't match the active step.

factual_errors: '263 rules keep working' (headline): facts say react-x/no-leaked-conditional-rendering crashed on 190 files and must be turned off, and migration adds new false positives (2 testing-library, 1 import, 1 no-unsafe-argument).
'Oxlint runs the same lint in 5.3 s': the 5.3 s run came after dropping the typed react-x rule and without the no-restricted-syntax selectors, so it is not the same lint.

'Oxlint's React, testing-library and local rules run as alpha JS plugins': facts say react (eslint-plugin-react), react-hooks, jsx-a11y, import and nextjs are built in; only react-x, react-jsx, testing-library and local rules are JS plugins.
'A format check took 2.3 s against Prettier's 10.2 s' (presented as a clean comparison): the 2.3 s oxfmt run flagged 1,028 of 1,030 files on the CRLF checkout, before the LF fix.
